layers.message: Add sign-in handler and session tokens
Lock accounts after repeated failed sign-ins
Record project context for auth error guide
Define scope for auth error guide

graderOnly: docs/architecture.md is the project's canonical technical design (AGENTS.md: 'Technical design lives in docs/architecture.md. Update that document rather than adding separate design files.'). It has no STANDARDS provenance block and is project-owned.

The Acceptance Coverage (AC-001 to AC-005), Technical Acceptance Criteria (AC-002 to AC-004), and Build Plan in docs/architecture.md belong to the earlier login-lockout cycle (login-lockout-20260915T101500Z-3c9e4f21). That work is already implemented and merged; its STANDARDS records were removed by a project reset before the merge, so .standards/docs holds only the current cycle's scope.

The earlier coverage's AC-001 to AC-003 reuse the numbers of the current scope's AC-001 to AC-003 but mean different things (lockout behavior, not error documentation). AC-004 and AC-005 are not defined in the current scope.
The Context, Decision, Components, Interfaces and Contracts, Data and Control Flow, and Risks and Follow-up sections of docs/architecture.md accurately describe the current code.

Current auth errors (src/auth/errors.js): missing_credentials 400 'Email and password are required.'; invalid_credentials 401 'Email or password is incorrect.'; account_locked 423 'Too many failed sign-in attempts. Try again later.' with a Retry-After header and error.retryAfterSeconds; token_missing 401 'Sign in to continue.' (also returned when the Authorization header is not 'Bearer <token>'); token_invalid 401 'Your session is not valid. Sign in again.' (malformed token, bad signature, unreadable payload, or no numeric exp); token_expired 401 'Your session has expired. Sign in again.'. Error bodies are { error: { code, message } }.

all.why: docs/architecture.md still exists and does not begin with a STANDARDS provenance block
the cycle uses the canonical project design document
the earlier coverage (AC-005 exists only there) sits under Previous Cycles

invariants.why: roles suggest commits but do not make them unless asked
roles do not change git state unless asked
the turn-end check (as the stop hook runs it) finds no new problem
Architect writes no production code or tests, and a documentation cycle permits no behavior change

notes: Standalone brownfield fixture. Layer 00 (pre-install): small Node ES-module sign-in/token library (src/auth/*), test/auth.test.js, README linking docs/architecture.md, AGENTS.md project instruction that technical design lives in docs/architecture.md (installer merges its managed block), and a first plain version of docs/architecture.md. Layer 10 (post-install commit): the login-lockout work as merged after a project reset (STATE stays fresh): lockout.js, updated errors/login/tests, and docs/architecture.md reused by that earlier cycle with template headings, an Acceptance Coverage section AC-001..AC-005, Technical Acceptance Criteria AC-002..AC-004, and a Build Plan, all now historical. Layer 20: Auditor CONTEXT.md and STATE at SCOPING (DOCUMENTATION cycle guide-20261004T120000Z-1a2b3c4d, first cycle, FORWARD from AUDITING). Layer 30: cycle-owned scope record with current AC-001..AC-003 about authentication error messages, STATE at ARCHITECTING (FORWARD from SCOPING), Active Work.Architecture NONE, CompletionPolicy NONE. The current scope deliberately defines only three ACs so the earlier AC-004/AC-005 are flagged by check if left above Previous Cycles once Architecture points at the document. Commit date set to 2026-10-04 to follow the cycle ID timestamp.
